## TL;DR

A review's running registration used to survive when its reviewer failed, was cancelled, or was adopted after a dead process, so `review again` kept answering "already running" until the server restarted. This change makes every exit path release the registration, makes `review cancel` clear it even when the process is already gone, adds a reaper that clears an old registration with no live reviewer once it passes the review timeout, and makes the refusal say whether the reviewer is running, finalizing, or still preparing, with a pid and start time where one exists. Round 2 fixed the completion fence and identity-guard bugs. Round 3 fixes a finalizing review entry whose process has already exited, which used to read as live forever. The scoped `repoos check --changed main` passed on this tree (exit 0, no failed steps, 237 of 237 test files passed).

## Work and rationale

The registration lives in `ReviewManager` (`src/server/review.ts`) as three things: a `runs` record for a preparing or spawned review, a `completions` fence for a finished review whose report is still being stored, and the runner entry in `AgentRunner` (`src/server/agents.ts`) for the reviewer process. `canRun` and the refusal read all three, so a leak in any one blocks every later review. I kept that model and added the missing release points rather than redesigning it.

Round 3 splits "an entry exists" from "a reviewer process is alive." Round 2 had `registration()` ask `runner.isRunning(key)`, which returns true for any entry, including one whose finalize has not settled after the child exited. That is the bug the review found. `AgentRunner.reviewProcessLive(taskId)` now reconciles dead agents, then returns true only for an entry that is not `finalizing`. `ReviewManager.registration()` uses it for liveness and reports a `RegistrationPhase` of `running`, `finalizing` (a finished reviewer or a completion fence), or `preparing`.

The reaper and the refusal read the phase. The reaper clears any registration that is not `running` once it outlives the review timeout. When it drops a stale finalize, it also calls `AgentRunner.abandonFinalizing(key)`. Without that call the runner entry survives, and `startTurn` refuses with "task is already running or finalizing". The refusal now says `pid N` only for a running reviewer, `reviewer exited, finalizing its report` for a finalize, and `preparing, no reviewer process yet` otherwise, so a human can tell stale from live.

`cancel()` calls `abandonFinalizing` after it stops the child, so a cancel also clears a finalize whose child is already gone. It still leaves the completion fence alone, as round 2 decided: that fence belongs to the finalize that set it.

Late finalize safety. `abandonFinalizing` removes the entry, so the finalize that was already running can settle later. `finalizeTurn` now removes its runner entry and its registry record only when the registered entry is still its own, so it cannot delete a newer review admitted under the same key.

Adopted reviews. The root cause of the reported incident is in `reconcileDeadAgents`, which used to skip every review entry. An adopted review whose process died has no `close` event, so its completion hook never fired. The skip now excludes only `finalizing`, which is round 2's fix.

Behaviour changes kept on purpose: a review whose worktree has vanished is now finalized as failed (close-out cancels reviews before it removes a worktree, so this only happens on an unexpected removal), and reconcile passes `exitedCleanly=false` for a review with a live child handle, which `finalizeReviewDone` does not read.

## Approaches tried

- Round 2 kept the finalizing entry as "live" because the finalize was still running. The review showed that a dead process plus a hung finalize refuses every later review until restart. Splitting liveness from existence fixed it without changing when finalize runs.
- I considered having the reaper clear the runner entry directly. Going through `abandonFinalizing` keeps the registry-record removal and drain in one place, next to the existing `removeRegistryEntry` logic.
- For the fake-runner tests I used a stateful fake: `isRunning` stays true until `abandonFinalizing` clears it. A static `() => true` would make the reaper's effect invisible.
- The real-runner test (`review-dead-adopted.test.ts`) marks an adopted entry `finalizing` and checks the liveness flag, then abandons it. I did not force a hang in the real finalize; that path is covered by the identity guard and the fake-runner tests.

## Challenges and blockers

- Several existing test files build `ReviewManager` on top of hand-written runner fakes. Those fakes needed the two new methods. I added them in `reload.test.ts` and `post-handoff-checkpoint-recovery.test.ts` with values matching each fake's `isRunning`.
- The first handoff failed on a stale check input, so I reran `repoos check`. It was not a code failure.
- In my runs, `refresh-evidence-route.test.ts` and some `ui-verification-config` cases failed intermittently, each time a different set. They touch git capture and timing, not the review registration. `post-handoff-checkpoint-recovery.test.ts` also failed once under a parallel load and passed on repeat runs. I did not fix these, and I did not prove they fail on `main`.
- `running()` still lists a finalizing review with its dead pid. Only the refusal and liveness read it, and both now bypass it, so I left `running()` alone rather than change its other callers.
- No human step is needed. I did not run a live reviewer or a real API outage here; the outage case is covered by the simulated rejecting reviewer.

## Key learnings

- Liveness and existence are different questions. An entry can exist after its process is gone, so any "is it running" check must ask about the process, not the entry.
- A registration is only as safe as its weakest release path. Every removal must check it is removing its own record, or a late settle deletes a newer run.
- Clearing one map is not enough. The reviewer registration, the runner entry and the durable registry record each block something different, so the reaper has to clear all of them.
- Stateful fakes make cleanup tests meaningful. A fake that never changes after the cleanup call can pass for the wrong reason.
